disposition: ANALYSIS ONLY. No file was moved, no file was deleted, and the evidence contract was not edited. This receipt supplies the evidence an adjudicator needs to choose a direction; it does not choose one, and the recommendation in it is labelled as a recommendation.
question: R1/packets/ and R1/tools/ are outside the evidence contract's roundLayout allowlist and are the only two structural blockers left in round-evidence R1. What is actually in them, what depends on them, and what would each remedy really cost?

contractFinding.observation: A case-insensitive search of evidence-contract/index.json for 'packet' and for 'tools' returns NOTHING. The contract does not know either directory.
contractFinding.correctionToAPriorFraming: The coordinator's brief suggested packets/ 'looks session-invented (it is absent from the contract's own enumeration)' while tools/ holds live instruments. Absence from the contract does not distinguish them: tools/ is equally absent. The real distinction is coupling, measured below, and it points the other way from what absence alone would suggest — tools/ is the one that cannot be moved, packets/ is the one that technically could.

packets.artifactClass: lane work packets — INPUT declarations. Common shape: schemaVersion, roundId, cohort, lane, laneClass, ownedFamilies, ownedFiles, observableDefect, applicableRubricDimensions. They declare what a lane owns and intends.
packets.executableCoupling: NONE. Nothing imports, requires, or loads a packet programmatically. They are pure data.

tools.artifactClass: live executable instruments — the probes and emitters that PRODUCE receipts.
tools.externalInvokers: NONE FOUND. No package.json script and nothing under packages/core/scripts or packages/showroom invokes these tools; they are run by hand. So migration would not break a pipeline — the damage is to evidence bindings, not to automation.

blastRadius.method: grep for the literal paths R1/tools and R1/packets across every .json, .mjs, .md, .ts and .tsx in the repository outside node_modules, then classify each hit as EXECUTABLE (a path the runtime loads or a guard enforces) or NARRATIVE (prose asserting where something lives).

executable.detail: 8 are structured `path` + `sha256` pairs inside harnessSelfHash / self-attestation blocks in cohort-1-capture-harness-self-test.json and cohort-1-i18n-gate.json. 1 is the `instrument` field of a FROZEN receipt.

packets.detail: 153 of the 159 are in inherited-entry-ledger-v2.json, almost all one repeated per-entry boilerplate: 'No packet under R1/packets/*.json lists this path in ownedFiles or filesActuallyChanged...'. The remaining 6 are in cohort-1-stressmatrix-completion-map.json. Every one of them ASSERTS A LOCATION, so all 159 become factually stale the moment the directory moves, even though none of them breaks anything at runtime.

hardBlockers.what: EXPECTED_ANCESTORS = ['tools','R1','wo-cra-23','quality-evidence','test-artifacts','core','packages']. deriveRepoRoot() walks this fixed chain and THROWS if any ancestor name does not match, index 0 being the tool's own parent directory — literally the string 'tools'.
hardBlockers.consequence: Moving these out of a directory named 'tools' makes deriveRepoRoot throw immediately. The guard is deliberately fail-closed — its own error text reads 'Refusing to guess a repo root'. It also says: 'if this tool moved, update EXPECTED_ANCESTORS in receipt-io.mjs to match.' So migration REQUIRES a source edit to a live instrument.
hardBlockers.note: The depth arithmetic would survive. Tools resolve the core root as path.resolve(HERE,'..','..','..','..','..') — five levels up from R1/tools. R1/receipts sits at the identical depth, so the computed root would still be correct. It is the NAME check, not the depth walk, that fires. A migration that only moved files and fixed nothing would fail loudly rather than silently, which is the good news in this finding.

hardBlockers.what: A FROZEN receipt whose `instrument` field is the literal path test-artifacts/quality-evidence/wo-cra-23/R1/tools/overlay-causality-probe.mjs, bound to FINAL_SHA f2091b2e92f10298..., mtimeEpoch 1785951047, sizeBytes 159415, plus a stabilityProof of three spaced samples by the coordinator and an independent 3/3 corroboration by the auditor.
hardBlockers.consequence: Content SHA and size survive a move, and `mv` on one filesystem preserves mtime, so three of the four bindings would still verify. The PATH would not. A frozen handoff that names a file which is no longer there is a broken record, and repairing it means editing frozen evidence.
hardBlockers.precision: This is a path-binding break, NOT a hash break. Stating it as 'the freeze is invalidated' would overclaim.

hardBlockers.what: 8 recorded path+sha256 pairs. These are SELF-attestations: each tool hashed itself, at that path, at run time.
hardBlockers.consequence: The hashes stay valid; the paths do not. Re-pointing them means either hand-editing evidence (which makes it no longer a machine self-attestation) or re-running the instruments to regenerate — and re-running is a new capture, against a frozen capture set.

options.summary: Move both directories into receipts/, the only plausible allowlisted destination.
costForTools: Requires editing tools/receipt-io.mjs (EXPECTED_ANCESTORS) — a source edit to a live instrument in the same family as a frozen one.
Breaks 8 self-attestation path records across 2 receipts.
Breaks the `instrument` path of 1 FROZEN receipt.
Repairing any of the above means editing frozen or machine-attested evidence by hand.
costForPackets: Makes 159 narrative citations factually stale, 153 of them in one ledger.
options.sharedCost: A CATEGORY ERROR in both cases. receipts/ means 'records of results'. A packet is an INPUT declaration and an instrument is an EXECUTABLE that produces receipts; neither is a receipt. Filing them there would satisfy the allowlist while making the taxonomy false — the same 'name it something it is not so the checker passes' failure class this round has spent itself unwinding elsewhere.
options.verdictState: Highest cost, and the only option that damages existing evidence.

options.summary: Leave both in place, record them as knowingly-outside-layout under a named deferral.
cost: Zero edits, zero risk, no evidence damaged.
round-evidence R1 stays valid:false permanently unless the contract changes, so R1 can never be sealed from this state.
options.verdictState: Cheapest, and safe, but it is a HOLDING state rather than a terminal one. It defers the same decision to whoever tries to seal the round.

options.summary: Add tools/ and/or packets/ to the roundLayout allowlist.
cost: One edit to evidence-contract/index.json — an adjudicator's artifact, explicitly not mine to touch.
Preserves every path, every hash, every frozen record, the fail-closed guard, and the taxonomy.

The real risk is precedent: the allowlist exists to stop arbitrary sprawl, so an amendment must be a deliberate decision that these are recognised artifact classes, not a rubber stamp to clear a blocker.
options.verdictState: Lowest damage. Cost is a governance decision rather than an evidence cost.

RECOMMENDATION.label: THIS IS A RECOMMENDATION, NOT A DECISION. The direction is the adjudicator's.
RECOMMENDATION.recommend: Option (c), contract amendment, for BOTH directories — but for one shared reason rather than two special cases.
reasoning: The allowlist is under-specified, not violated. A round of this shape legitimately produces three artifact classes: INPUTS (lane packets), INSTRUMENTS (the probes that generate evidence), and OUTPUTS (receipts, captures, recordings). The allowlist names outputs richly and does not name the other two at all. packets/ and tools/ are not sprawl; they are two unnamed classes doing exactly what their names say.

Option (a) is the only one that destroys evidence, and it destroys the most load-bearing kind: machine self-attestations and a frozen instrument binding. Paying evidence damage to satisfy a naming rule inverts the purpose of the rule.

Filing an executable under receipts/ would make the tree pass the checker while making it describe itself falsely. That is the two-authorities defect wearing different clothes: the checker would say 'receipt' and the filesystem would hold an instrument.

I do NOT recommend the asymmetric split (amend for tools/, migrate packets/ since it is technically movable). It buys one fewer allowlist entry at the price of 159 stale citations and a second category error. Technically-movable is not the same as should-be-moved.
RECOMMENDATION.ifTheAdjudicatorWantsMinimumContractSurf: The defensible fallback is (c) for tools/ and (b) for packets/ — amend for the class that cannot move without evidence damage, and hold packets/ as a named deferral pending a later decision on whether inputs belong in the round layout at all. This still leaves round-evidence invalid, so it does not unblock sealing.
RECOMMENDATION.notRecommended: Option (a) for tools/ under any framing. The fail-closed guard, the frozen instrument path and the 8 self-attestations make it the most expensive path available, and its cost lands on the evidence rather than on the contract.

establishes: A complete file-level inventory of both directories.
A measured, not estimated, blast radius: 16 citations across 9 receipts for tools/, 159 across 2 for packets/, each classified executable vs narrative.
Three named hard blockers to migration, each located to a file and line where applicable.
That no automation invokes these tools, so migration risk is to evidence bindings and not to any pipeline.
doesNotEstablish: Any decision. The direction is not chosen here.
Any claim about the two deferred artifacts (manifest.json, SHA256SUMS), which remain correctly deferred until contents freeze.
Any verdict on the work order. This receipt describes results only; roadmap/registry.json remains the sole authority for work-order state.

SUPERSEDED_BY_ADJUDICATION.ruling: The coordinator adjudicated BOUNDED FORWARD MIGRATION — option (a). Options (b) preserved-invalid and (c) contract amendment were NOT taken. My recommendation of (c) was not followed, and that is the adjudicator's call, correctly made outside this receipt.
SUPERSEDED_BY_ADJUDICATION.effectOnThisReceipt: Every R1/tools and R1/packets path named ABOVE describes the PRE-MIGRATION state and has deliberately been left unrewritten — rewriting them would make the analysis describe a layout that never posed the problem it analyses. Read this receipt as a historical record of why the migration was shaped the way it was.
SUPERSEDED_BY_ADJUDICATION.executed: See cohort-1-outside-layout-migration.json for the manifest of what moved, what was re-verified, and the one source edit required.
SUPERSEDED_BY_ADJUDICATION.oneAnalysisFindingProvedDecisive: The claim above that migration would force an edit to the FROZEN instrument held only for a NESTED move. Because R1/receipts sits at the same depth as the old R1/tools, a FLAT move preserved every depth constant and the frozen instrument was never touched. The migration was therefore materially cheaper than option (a) was costed at here.
